doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: His father's modest career in swing bands around Detroit
summary: His father played gigs around Detroit as a teenager but lacked the chops to go professional and quit after World War II.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did he talk about what those experiences were like with you? Playing with the big bands?
Yes. He did. He never really got too far with it, I mean he played just, really, when he was kind of a teenager is when he did most of his playing. And he picked it up and started

playing some gigs around Detroit, which is, I’m from near Detroit, and he played with some German bands and some swing combos and big bands, and he talked about it but he said he’d never really had the chops to really make it as a professional. He just was close but no cigar. But he always loved the music. After World War II he gave up playing just to go into other professions — real estate and different things like that.
